newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's flood toll rises, more rain on the way.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's flood toll rises, more rain on the way.

text.p: The death toll from recent flooding in Vietnam has risen to 342 and a tropical depression is expected to bring more heavy rain to the hard-hit central provinces over the weekend, relief authorities said on Friday.
The U.N.-sponsored Disaster Management Unit (DMU) said flooding had claimed 180 lives in the Mekong Delta and 162 in the central provinces, where 44 people were still missing.
In the delta, Vietnam's rice-bowl, tens of thousands of people are in need of emergency relief and close to 800,000 houses have been either submerged or damaged by water.
DMU said some 258,000 hectares (637,500 acres) of the area's paddy fields were submerged, more than 11 percent of which had been completely destroyed.

The unit's latest figures took the nationwide death toll from natural disasters over the past six months to 921 and the cost of damages to around $620 million, making this one of the worst years on record for typhoons, cyclones and floods.

The meteorological office in Hanoi said Tropical Storm Ernie, which has been swirling off the southern central coast with winds of up to 74 km (46 miles) per hour since Thursday, had now lost momentum.

It said the system, now a tropical depression with winds of 39-49 km (24-30 miles) per hour, would hit land on Friday night, bringing rains to six coastal provinces stretching from Quang Ngai to Binh Thuan.
